sections.h2: The 131st Amendment fell 54 votes short in the Lok Sabha

chart.title: Yes votes reached 298 of the 352 needed; 230 voted no
chart.sub: Votes on the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, Lok Sabha, 17 April 2026.
chart.source: Drishti IAS; The South First; Vision IAS.

sections.means: The bill would have enlarged the Lok Sabha to 850 seats and brought women's reservation forward, but it was defeated.
sections.todo: Parliament must agree a seat formula before Census 2027 unfreezes allocation, so the next bill has to win the support the 131st lacked.

sections.h2: Governors: courts dropped their own timelines, so only Parliament can set them

chart.title: Courts set timelines in 2025, then dropped them, leaving the fix to Parliament
events: Sarkaria Commission asks for time limits on Governors' assent to bills
Supreme Court sets timelines in the Tamil Nadu case
Presidential Reference opinion: no judicially imposed timelines, no deemed assent

sections.means: Governors' assent has been recommended for reform since 1988, and the November 2025 opinion left no court-set deadline.
sections.todo: A fixed timeline for assent under Article 200 needs a constitutional amendment, so Parliament must draft one.

sections.h2: Two bills in committee have had their deadlines extended into the Winter Session

chart.title: Both committee bills got deadline extensions into the 2026 Winter Session
events: One Nation One Election bill (129th) introduced by 269 votes to 196 and sent to a JPC
JPC on the 130th Amendment defers adopting its draft report
Lok Sabha extends the 129th Bill's deadline to the first day of the last week of Winter Session
Lok Sabha extends the 130th Bill's deadline to the last week of Winter Session

sections.means: The One Nation One Election and 130th Amendment bills are still with joint committees, and neither has reported.
sections.todo: Both committees need to table reports by the Winter Session deadline, since a third extension would leave the bills unresolved.
